name: TN-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+13 district lean in a Republican-favorable environment
Fundraising gap: Garrett about $2.4M raised vs Croley about $104K
Open seat after John Rose's retirement, but terrain still strongly favors the GOP
Prediction markets price Democratic odds near 4%
model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean, a Republican-favorable environment, and a roughly twenty-to-one fundraising gap leave Mike Croley with no evident path, and betting markets give Democrats only about a four percent chance. The open seat removes incumbency protection but does little to change the underlying partisanship.
model.watch: A major Garrett misstep or scandal, or a sharp late national shift toward Democrats, is the likeliest route to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John Rose (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Tennessee's 6th District is an open seat after Republican John Rose retired to run for governor, but the underlying terrain remains heavily Republican. The district leans about thirteen points toward the GOP, and this cycle's political environment also favors Republicans. Johnny Garrett enters the general election as the clear favorite on the Republican side.

The fundraising gap is stark: Garrett has raised roughly $2.4 million with outside groups adding to his side, while Democrat Mike Croley has raised about $104,000 with minimal cash on hand. No public polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, money, and betting markets, which put Democratic odds near four percent. Two independents are also on the ballot with little visible support. The main open question is the size of the Republican margin rather than the winner.
